title: Towards Uncertainty-aware Robotic Perception via Mixed-signal BNN Engine Leveraging Probabilistic Quantum Tunneling
problem: Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) provide uncertainty quantification essential for safety-critical robotic perception, but traditional software BNNs have prohibitively high hardware overhead and latency, restricting real-time deployment on resource-constrained robots.
motivation: Autonomous robots in unstructured environments require both high accuracy and uncertainty estimates to detect data noise vs. model uncertainty; real-time perception demands efficient hardware.
method: Mixed-signal hardware accelerator leverages probabilistic quantum tunneling in fully depleted silicon-on-insulator (FDSOI) transistors to generate Gaussian random variables efficiently (200 fJ/sample, r=0.997 correlation). Parallel BNN architecture uses this compact randomness source for low-latency probabilistic inference.
key_novelty: Using FDSOI quantum tunneling for efficient, on-chip random variable generation enabling hardware-efficient Bayesian neural network acceleration.
contributions: Mixed-signal BNN accelerator achieving 10^3-10^4x latency reduction vs. software
FDSOI quantum tunneling-based RNG at 200 fJ/sample with high-quality Gaussian outputs
Uncertainty-aware visual localization with 4.5x improved resampling efficiency at same accuracy
limitations: Evaluation primarily on underwater vehicle localization; scalability to larger robotic applications and broader perception tasks not discussed.
